--- Page 1 (Beckerman_55a) --- Dear Folks and Ruth: This is the letter I thought I might not have to write you -- but I was wrong so here it is. There has been a slight change of plans and accordingly I won't be home as soon as you or I had expected. You recall that I told you that officers could be held for two months after they become eligible for separation. That's what's happened to me. As soon as I found out that the point score was being lowered I lost no time in asking for immediate separation as of 1 December. That's what I wrote you about last week. But my application came back marked "essential". That means that I will be held for two months after 1 Dec before being made available by my headquarters for separation. That brings me to 1 Feb. Of course that is subject to change at any time but frankly I think that the verdict will hold true to the last day. I'm sorry but that's the whole truth. I could be on my way right now if circumstances had been different. But that is the way it is right now. Until Feb 1st comes around I'll still be here. Hope this doesn't come as too much of a surprise. I didn't try arguing with the colonel after he made his decision. Two more months really won't make too much difference after all this time. Besides have had more than my share of good breaks up to now so there's nothing to be too disappointed about. It so happens that my job has become even more important since the war ended and I think I could be off some time to the next sixtydays. There's one very big picture. I will tell you about it, but then again don't won't you to pace too much weight on it until I can give you further details. You know that I have been working hard and but budgets have been --- Page 2 (Beckerman_55b) --- Pacific for about two years and have been able to accumulate quite a bit of information about the business. Well, you have read of Congress demanding reduction in WD spending as soon as the war ended. We are now working on post war budget schedules for activities of the army in the Pacific area. This project has to be completed soon and a delegation from our office must be in Washington on 1 Feb to explain and just- ify our activities to certain congressional committees. I'm going to try to get on that delegation. Since I'll have to work on the project until completed I figure I might as well see the whole thing thru. However, as I said, I don't know whether I'll be able to make it. It would be interesting, and more important it would mean that I would return to the US via a comfortable plane trip. That's a factor I'm strongly considering. So right now it stands as follows.(1) I will not be able to get out of the army before 1 Feb. (2) I may be able to leave here slightly before 1 Feb for a short tour of duty at Washington and then head for the separation center as soon as the duty is completed.... Wish you would write to me and let me know how you feel about this thing. Abe should be on his way home by now. I received a letter from you earlier this week. That's all for now folks. Will write you again in a few days. Still feeling in the chips: everything OK.. Love and regards....
